name: Titanium Advanced Menu Rules
author: Admin Plugins

sections.description:
Turn your WordPress menu into smart navigation. Show the right menu items to members, customers, visitors, and admins — automatically. Titanium also helps catch missing or unassigned menus before your visitors do.

Your menu is one of the first things people use on your website. If every visitor sees the same links, your navigation can quickly become crowded, confusing, or irrelevant.

Titanium Advanced Menu Rules helps you create cleaner, smarter WordPress menus by showing or hiding menu items based on login status, user roles, pages, posts, and membership rules. The Free version gives you practical visibility rules inside the standard WordPress menu editor. The Pro version adds advanced condition groups, membership plugin integrations, and optional linked page protection for sites that need deeper control.

Manage everything from Appearance → Menus. No theme editing. No custom snippets. No separate menu builder.

What Titanium Advanced Menu Rules helps you do

  • Show account links only to logged-in users.
  • Hide login or register links after a visitor signs in.
  • Show admin, editor, member, donor, or customer links only to the right roles.
  • Create cleaner navigation for public visitors and logged-in users.
  • Show or hide menu items on selected pages or posts.
  • Build membership-aware menus for supported membership plugins.
  • Catch missing or unassigned menu locations before they confuse visitors.
  • Keep using the normal WordPress menu editor you already know.

Why smarter menus matter

A menu should guide people, not distract them.

Many WordPress sites grow over time: membership areas, account pages, customer dashboards, donation pages, downloads, support links, admin links, private content, and special offers. When all of those links are shown to everyone, the menu becomes harder to understand.

Titanium Advanced Menu Rules helps keep your navigation focused. Visitors see the links that make sense for them, while unnecessary menu items can stay hidden until they are relevant.

Free features

Titanium Advanced Menu Rules Free includes practical menu visibility tools for WordPress sites that need reliable, easy-to-manage navigation control.

Show or hide individual menu items

Choose whether each menu item should be shown or hidden when its rule matches. This makes it possible to create different navigation experiences without duplicating entire menus.

Logged-in visitor rules

Show or hide menu items for logged-in users. This is useful for account links, dashboards, member areas, profile pages, downloads, support areas, and any navigation that should only appear after login.

Logged-out visitor rules

Show or hide menu items for logged-out visitors. This is useful for login links, registration links, join links, donation links, pricing links, or public calls to action that should disappear once the visitor is already logged in.

WordPress role rules

Target menu items by WordPress user role. You can show or hide links for administrators, editors, authors, subscribers, customers, custom membership roles, donor roles, or any other role registered on your site.

Role is / role is not logic

Use positive or negative role matching. For example, show a link only to selected roles, or hide a link from selected roles while keeping it visible to everyone else.

Page-based menu rules

Show or hide menu items when the visitor is viewing selected WordPress pages. This helps create page-specific navigation without building separate menus for every section of the site.

Post-based menu rules

Show or hide menu items when the visitor is viewing selected WordPress posts. This is useful for blogs, guides, announcements, protected content areas, and content-specific navigation.

Page is / page is not logic

Display menu items only on selected pages, or hide them on selected pages. This is useful for landing pages, checkout pages, account pages, member pages, and special content areas.

Post is / post is not logic

Display menu items only on selected posts, or hide them on selected posts. This gives more control around individual posts without editing templates.

Server-side menu filtering

Hidden menu items are removed before the menu HTML is printed. They are not simply hidden with CSS, which keeps front-end output cleaner.

Works inside the standard WordPress menu editor

Rules are managed directly inside Appearance → Menus. You do not need to replace your theme navigation or learn a separate menu builder.

Searchable page and post selectors

Search for pages or posts directly from the menu item settings. This is easier than scrolling through long content lists on larger sites.

Role selection helpers

Role selection controls help you configure role-based rules faster, especially on sites with many custom roles.

Menu diagnostics and location warnings

Titanium can warn you when important menu setup is missing, such as when no menu is assigned or a menu location is not properly connected. This helps catch navigation setup problems before visitors notice them.

Header, mobile, and footer menu awareness

The plugin is built for real WordPress menu locations, including common header, mobile, and footer menu setups that use standard WordPress menu output.

Import from Nav Menu Roles

If the Nav Menu Roles plugin is active, Titanium Advanced Menu Rules can detect compatible rules and help import them.

Import from User Menus

If the User Menus plugin is active, Titanium Advanced Menu Rules can detect compatible rules and help import them.

Safe import review flow

Import tools include a review step and can detect existing Titanium Advanced Menu Rules settings, so you can decide whether imported rules should replace existing rules.

Locked Pro feature previews

The Free version shows locked previews of advanced Pro controls so you can understand what is available before upgrading, without running Pro-only logic in the Free version.

Pro features

Titanium Advanced Menu Rules Pro is available separately for sites that need more advanced logic, membership-aware navigation, and optional protection for the linked WordPress content behind menu items.

The Free version controls menu visibility. Pro adds deeper control for more complex sites.

Advanced condition groups

Create multiple rule groups for a single menu item. This makes it possible to build more flexible rules for sites where simple visibility logic is not enough.

AND logic inside groups

Combine multiple conditions inside the same group. For example, show a menu item only when the visitor is logged in AND has a selected role AND is viewing a selected page.

OR logic between groups

Create alternative rule groups for the same menu item. For example, show a menu item to Gold members OR administrators OR visitors viewing a specific page.

Combined role, login, page, and post logic

Use login status, WordPress roles, pages, and posts together in one advanced rule setup. This is useful for sites with different user types and different content areas.

Advanced Show / Hide control

Build more precise Show and Hide rules. This helps when a menu item should appear only in very specific situations, or disappear only for certain visitors.

WordPress role conditions

Use WordPress role conditions inside advanced Pro groups. This supports standard roles and custom roles created by membership plugins, eCommerce plugins, role editor plugins, or custom code.

Role is / role is not operators

Use positive or negative role matching inside advanced condition groups. This is useful when a menu item should be available to most users except one role, or only available to a small set of roles.

Login status conditions

Use logged-in or logged-out status inside advanced condition groups. This can be combined with roles, pages, posts, and membership conditions.

Page conditions

Target selected WordPress pages inside advanced condition groups. This is useful for landing pages, account pages, support pages, dashboard pages, member areas, and section-specific navigation.

Post conditions

Target selected WordPress posts inside advanced condition groups. This helps when navigation should change around specific articles, guides, announcements, or individual content items.

Membership plugin conditions

Pro adds membership-aware menu visibility rules for supported membership plugins. This lets you show or hide menu items based on active membership plans, levels, or subscriptions instead of relying only on WordPress roles.

Supported membership integrations include:

  • Paid Memberships Pro
  • MemberPress
  • WooCommerce Memberships
  • Restrict Content / Restrict Content Pro
  • Paid Member Subscriptions

Paid Memberships Pro level rules

Show or hide menu items by active Paid Memberships Pro membership level. This is useful for Silver, Gold, Platinum, VIP, donor, course, download, or member area navigation.

MemberPress membership rules

Show or hide menu items based on MemberPress memberships. This helps create navigation for different paid plans, protected areas, and member-only links.

WooCommerce Memberships plan rules

Show or hide menu items based on WooCommerce Memberships plans. This is useful for stores with member-only products, account areas, wholesale links, or customer-specific navigation.

Restrict Content / Restrict Content Pro rules

Show or hide menu items based on Restrict Content membership levels. This helps sites using Restrict Content or Restrict Content Pro keep navigation aligned with membership access.

Paid Member Subscriptions plan rules

Show or hide menu items based on Paid Member Subscriptions plans. This helps subscription sites display the right links for the right plan level.

Role + membership logic

Combine WordPress roles and membership conditions together. For example, show a menu item only to logged-in users who have a selected membership level and a selected WordPress role.

Membership + page logic

Combine membership conditions with page or post conditions. This allows navigation to change depending on both the visitor’s membership and the content they are viewing.

Linked Page Protection

Pro can optionally protect the WordPress page or post linked from a menu item. This helps prevent visitors from accessing the linked content directly by typing or opening the URL when the same menu visibility rules say they should not have access.

Direct URL protection for linked content

Free controls whether a menu link is visible. Pro can also control what happens when someone tries to open the linked WordPress content directly.

Per-menu-item protection

Linked Page Protection can be enabled per menu item, so you can choose exactly which linked pages or posts should be protected.

Global Linked Page Protection setting

Pro includes a global setting for linked content protection, allowing consistent protection behavior across protected menu items.

Administrator bypass option

Pro includes controls to avoid locking administrators out of protected content while testing or managing site rules.

Global denied access action

Choose what should happen when a visitor is denied access to protected linked content. This gives site owners more control over the visitor experience.

Per-menu denied access override

Override the global denied access behavior for individual protected menu items. This is useful when one protected page should redirect differently from another.

Redirect to homepage

Denied visitors can be sent to the homepage when they do not match the required rule conditions.

Redirect to selected page

Denied visitors can be sent to a selected WordPress page. This is useful for login pages, pricing pages, upgrade pages, donation pages, account pages, or custom explanation pages.

404 handling

Denied visitors can be shown a 404 response. This is useful when you do not want protected content URLs to appear accessible.

Built-in 404 page option

Pro includes a built-in 404 handling option for sites where the theme only shows a basic not found screen.

Use site/theme 404 page option

If your site already has a custom 404 page, Pro can use the site/theme 404 handling instead.

404 fallback protection

Selectable 404 handling includes fallback behavior so the denied access response remains controlled even when theme behavior is limited.

Membership system page bypass

Pro can skip membership plugin system pages so important membership pages, account pages, checkout pages, registration pages, and payment pages are not accidentally blocked by linked page protection.

Delayed redirect priority

Pro can run after other redirects, allowing membership plugins, security plugins, or custom redirect snippets to handle their own redirects first when needed.

Custom excluded paths

Add paths that should be excluded from linked page protection. This helps avoid conflicts with special URLs, plugin endpoints, checkout flows, account areas, and custom site logic.

Internal custom link resolving

Linked Page Protection can work with internal custom links that resolve to WordPress content on the same site, not only standard page/post menu items.

Advanced compatibility controls

Pro includes settings designed to reduce conflicts with membership plugins, redirect logic, security plugins, and custom site behavior.

Beta update opt-in

Pro users can opt into beta update offers when beta builds are available through Freemius. This is optional and intended for users who want to test upcoming fixes or improvements.

Priority Pro email support

Pro licenses include priority Pro email support for Titanium Advanced Menu Rules.

Free vs Pro summary

Free is ideal when you want cleaner menu visibility based on login status, WordPress roles, selected pages, and selected posts.

Pro is ideal when your site needs advanced condition groups, membership plugin rules, direct URL linked page protection, custom denied access handling, and deeper compatibility controls.

Important note about menu visibility and content protection

The Free version controls menu visibility. It removes hidden menu items from the rendered menu output, but it does not protect the linked page or post from direct URL access.

If you need the linked WordPress page or post to be protected from direct access using the same menu rules, use Titanium Advanced Menu Rules Pro with Linked Page Protection enabled.

Built for practical WordPress admin workflows

Titanium Advanced Menu Rules is designed to work with the standard WordPress menu editor. Rules are managed where menu items are already edited, so site owners do not need to rebuild their navigation in a separate interface.

The plugin is especially useful for:

  • Membership sites
  • Donation sites
  • Online communities
  • WooCommerce customer areas
  • Course sites
  • Download sites
  • Client portals
  • Private content areas
  • Sites with multiple user roles
  • Sites with different public and logged-in navigation

External services

This plugin connects to external services only on the plugin’s admin screens when an administrator opens the Upgrade / pricing page or starts the checkout flow.

AdminPlugins pricing API

This plugin connects to the AdminPlugins pricing API at https://adminplugins.com/wp-json/amr-freemius/v1/pricing to load the current public plan prices, license limits, discount state, and checkout URLs shown on the Upgrade page. The request is made from the WordPress admin area when an administrator opens or refreshes the plugin pricing page. The plugin sends a standard server-side HTTP GET request. No menu rules, site content, users, passwords, or license keys are sent by this request. If the administrator adds no_cache=1 to the current admin URL, the plugin also sends no_cache=1 to refresh the local pricing cache.

This service is provided by AdminPlugins: Terms of Service: https://adminplugins.com/terms-and-conditions/ Privacy Policy: https://adminplugins.com/privacy-policy/

Freemius SDK and Checkout

This plugin uses the Freemius SDK for optional Pro licensing, account management, software updates, and checkout. The plugin loads the Freemius Checkout JavaScript from https://checkout.freemius.com/js/v1/ on the plugin Upgrade / pricing page so administrators can open the secure checkout overlay when choosing a Pro plan. sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/titanium-advanced-menu-rules directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Appearance → Menus.
  4. Open a menu item.
  5. Configure the Titanium Advanced Menu Rules settings for that menu item.
  6. Save the menu.
sections.faq:
Where do I manage the menu rules?

Go to Appearance → Menus and open a menu item. Titanium Advanced Menu Rules adds visibility controls directly inside each menu item.

Does the Free version support WordPress roles?

Yes. The Free version can show or hide menu items for selected WordPress roles.

Can I hide menu items from logged-in users?

Yes. You can show or hide menu items based on whether the visitor is logged in or logged out.

Can I show a menu item only on selected pages?

Yes. The Free version supports page-based rules and post-based rules.

Are hidden menu items only hidden with CSS?

No. Hidden menu items are removed server-side before the menu HTML is printed.

Does Titanium help if my menu is not assigned?

Yes. Titanium includes admin-side diagnostics and warnings to help catch missing or unassigned menus before visitors notice them.

Does the Free version protect the linked page from direct access?

No. The Free version controls menu visibility only. It does not protect the linked page or post if someone opens the URL directly.

How can I protect the linked page from direct URL access?

Titanium Advanced Menu Rules Pro includes optional Linked Page Protection, which can protect linked WordPress pages and posts using the same menu rule logic.

Does Pro support membership plugins?

Yes. Pro includes membership conditions for Paid Memberships Pro, MemberPress, WooCommerce Memberships, Restrict Content / Restrict Content Pro, and Paid Member Subscriptions.

Can Pro combine multiple conditions?

Yes. Pro supports advanced condition groups with AND logic inside groups and OR logic between groups.

Can I redirect denied visitors?

Yes. Pro includes denied access actions such as homepage redirect, selected page redirect, and 404 handling.

Can I import rules from another menu visibility plugin?

The plugin includes import tools for supported menu visibility plugins such as Nav Menu Roles and User Menus when compatible data is detected.

Does this work with block themes and the Navigation block?

Titanium Advanced Menu Rules is designed for standard WordPress menus managed under Appearance → Menus and rendered through WordPress menu output. Sites using block theme Navigation blocks may behave differently depending on how the theme outputs navigation.

Will this delete my menus?

No. The plugin stores visibility settings for menu items. It does not delete your WordPress menus.

Can administrators still manage hidden menu items?

Yes. Rules affect front-end menu output. Menu items remain manageable in the WordPress admin.
